record_identity.title: Governance Provenance Must Follow the Amendment

report_title: Governance Provenance Must Follow the Amendment
case_descriptor: Lessons from amendment-level provenance repair within the broader institutional-governance-drift failure
summary: Document-level authorship and stewardship are insufficient to reconstruct how governance changed. Material amendments need their own preserved change summary, time, responsible agent or process, model, reviewer, and reference state so that later readers can distinguish founding authority from subsequent modification and detect silent doctrinal drift.
what_happened: FM-0034 documented a recurring institutional pattern in which material safeguards can lose authority or effect through succession, restructuring, policy revision, commercial pressure, sovereign contracting, or institutional capture.
Review of the Caelestis corpus identified a narrower internal weakness: static authorship and review blocks did not provide amendment-level provenance for later changes across governed instruments.

CAM migrated governed amendment ledgers to seven-column provenance, preserved historical amendment data and hashes, updated parsers and validators, and verified deterministic reconstruction; broader constitutional persistence and capture-resistance controls remain unresolved.
governance_misconception: Naming the document's author, steward, or current reviewer was treated as sufficient provenance for every later amendment.
Governance legitimacy was treated as inhering in the instrument as a whole rather than requiring traceability of each material change.
Historical amendment rows could be migrated or normalised without strict preservation of their existing versions, summaries, timestamps, and reference hashes.
Improved provenance was treated as capable of solving the broader problem of safeguard durability, succession, capture, notice, appeal, and equivalent successor protection.
abstracted_learning: Governance provenance must be amendment-granular. Each material change should remain attributable to its change, time, responsible agent or process, model, reviewer, and reference state, with deterministic tooling that can verify source-to-registry completeness without rewriting historical substance.
integrated_learning: Document-level authorship does not establish amendment-level responsibility.
Static stewardship or review blocks can obscure which later actor, model, or process changed the operative doctrine.
Historical amendment content and hashes should be preserved during provenance migration.
Parsers, validators, repair tools, and registries should identify canonical fields by header meaning rather than fragile column position.
Generated indexes must remain reconstructable from governed source instruments.
Amendment provenance improves accountability but does not itself create succession resistance, independent oversight, notice, appeal, capture resistance, or an equivalent successor safeguard.
risk_if_not_integrated: Later amendments may inherit legitimacy from founding authors or reviewers who did not make or approve them.
Human and AI contributions may become indistinguishable, impairing responsibility, audit, correction, and historical interpretation.
Silent doctrinal drift or governance capture may be harder to detect because the operative change cannot be tied to a responsible amendment event.
Generated registries may diverge from governed source instruments without a deterministic completeness check.
Provenance reform may be overstated as a full repair while substantive safeguard durability remains unresolved.
future_application: Constitutions, policies, standards, and governance corpora
Model cards, safety frameworks, and release policies
generalisation_boundary: This lesson does not require public disclosure of protected deliberations, make every editorial correction constitutionally material, or establish that provenance alone prevents governance erosion. It applies where a material amendment changes operative authority, safeguards, obligations, classifications, rights, oversight, or interpretation and later accountability depends on knowing how that change occurred.
